column1: # Rule: a box along a tiling row on a node holding 8 or 16 bits (the across pass of a blur; the down pass is the same on
# columns). R = radius (intensity W / 256 aspect), h = ceil(R - 0.5), n = 2h + 1 texels, the two ends weigh c = R - (h - 0.5).
# Reads are bilinear with the weight in 1/256ths and round half up to a 16-bit step.
# n = 3: centre + c (left + right). n = 5: centre + (1 + c) (read(inner, end) on each side), weight round(c/(1+c) 256)/256.
# Wider: the end at an odd position (else the last) is read alone, weight c; the other end pair is such a read, weight 1 + c;
# between, a pyramid of the row's aligned pairs, each level held in the node's format (16 bits: half up; 8 bits: the 8-bit
# rule), top level ceil(log2(n - 1)) - 1. At each level: an odd count: the texel that doesn't line up alone (the first if
# odd, else the last); even and aligned: next level; even and not: the two end texels alone and next level between; two
# unaligned texels read without rounding. The sum / 2R goes through the node's rounding (node_hold.tsv).
# Applies to tiling rows of a power-of-two width wider than n; R <= 0.5 changes nothing.
# Source: measurement "One-effect projects" > "What nodes hold and how they read" ("Box blur along an axis on an integer
# node"), and "Node rules" (across, the node's rounding, then down).
# Tolerance: exact, in levels of the node's format.
# Columns: format = 8 or 16 (bits the node holds); width = texels in the row; radius = R in texels; input, output = the row's
# levels (k/255 or k/65535), left to right, the row repeating at its ends.
